clue.text: Crewman holding all the cards? Just one person's

parts.note: a deck is a full pack, all the cards there are
a hand is the set of cards held by just one player

explanation.surface: A sailor seems to have the whole pack, then turns out to own only his own share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' joins the pieces: the whole pack is a DECK, one player's share is a HAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A deckhand is an ordinary member of a ship's crew who works on deck.

clue.text: Cut when rewritten

indicators.note: rewritten says the letters of the word before it are set down in a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction about when a passage was trimmed during a rewrite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' turns WHEN into HEWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewn is the past participle of hew, meaning chopped or cut, as in hewn timber.

clue.text: Primate includes a bishop in blessing

indicators.note: in puts the short pieces inside the word for blessing

parts.note: a boon is a blessing or benefit
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An ape somehow takes in a churchman as part of a benediction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places AB within BOON, after its first letter; 'includes' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A baboon is a large African monkey, a member of the primate order.

clue.text: As I say, somehow crossing river in ancient kingdom

indicators.note: crossing means the rearranged letters straddle the abbreviation for river
somehow says the letters of the phrase before it are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Someone muses about a river running through a long-vanished realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' turns AS I SAY into ASSYIA; 'crossing' puts R inside it to give ASSY-R-IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Assyria was a great empire of the ancient Near East, centred on the Tigris.

clue.text: Figure in plane caught in old muddle

indicators.note: in puts the cricket abbreviation inside the pair of words around it

parts.note: a tangle is a muddle or confusion
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A shape on an aircraft gets snared in some ancient mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure in plane' reads like something on an aeroplane but means a plane figure in geometry. 'in' puts C between O and TANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An octangle is an eight-sided polygon, a flat shape in two-dimensional geometry.

clue.text: Spy setter wandering in shopping area

parts.note: James Bond is the fictional British spy

indicators.note: wandering says the letters of the word before it stray into another order

explanation.surface: A secret agent, together with the crossword's compiler, roams a retail district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' turns SETTER into STREET. BOND STREET is an upmarket shopping street in London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: Bond Street is a famous London street of luxury shops, so a shopping area.

clue.text: Cover using precautionary phrase, in a word

definitions.meaning: to encase something is to enclose or cover it
the phrase '...', as a precaution, written as a single word

explanation.surface: Something hidden behind a phrase used as insurance.
explanation.definitionFit: To incase, a variant of encase, is to put in a case or cover; split, it gives the precautionary 'in case'.

clue.text: Old king putting drink back in lists of options

indicators.note: in puts the turned drink inside the word for lists of options

parts.note: menus are lists of options, on a computer or in a restaurant

indicators.note: back says the drink is read from right to left

parts.note: ale is a drink, a kind of beer

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch puts his drink back amid choices on the bill of fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ALE into ELA, and 'in' puts it in MENUS: MEN-ELA-US.
explanation.definitionFit: Menelaus was the legendary king of Sparta, husband of Helen, in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Make king take rook, perhaps, then knight

parts.note: a rook is a kind of crow, hence 'perhaps'
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A chess move: capture a rook, then a knight, to promote a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess surface misleads: the rook is the bird, a member of the crow family.
explanation.definitionFit: To crown someone is to install them as monarch in a coronation ceremony.

clue.text: Hide from vicious king

indicators.note: from says the answer is drawn out of the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone takes cover from a cruel monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the two words: viciou-S KIN-g.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is an animal's skin, especially a tanned one.

clue.text: King of kings, many said foolishly, put on a little weight

indicators.note: put on says the rearranged letters are added after the weight

parts.note: oz is the abbreviation for ounce, a small weight

indicators.note: foolishly says the letters of the words before it are set out in a silly order

explanation.surface: A self-styled supreme ruler, it was widely said, had gained a few pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' rearranges MANY SAID, and 'put on' adds the result after OZ. In Shelley's poem the statue's pedestal reads 'My name is Ozymandias, King of Kings'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozymandias, the Greek name for Rameses II, calls himself king of kings in Shelley's sonnet.

clue.text: King's names for religious reformer

definitions.meaning: the given names of Dr King, the American civil rights leader
the German monk whose ninety-five theses began the Protestant Reformation

explanation.surface: A civil rights leader's forenames belong to a church reformer.
explanation.walkthrough: Martin Luther King Jr was named after the sixteenth-century reformer.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Luther led the Protestant Reformation, and his name forms the first names of Martin Luther King.

clue.text: Representatives who should become less narrow-minded

definitions.meaning: commercial ... are sales representatives on the road
travel broadens the mind, so those who go abroad ought to grow more open

explanation.surface: Salespeople who ought to grow broader in outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Sales reps journey from client to client, and the saying holds that travel broadens the mind.

clue.text: King at Hereford, in part to collect harvest

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A monarch at a cathedral city brings in the crops.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the words: K-ING AT HER-eford. Hereford is an English cathedral city in farming country.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingather is to gather in, especially to bring in a harvest.

clue.text: Some of our kings and English duke died in conflicts

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for died inside the word for conflicts

parts.note: wars are armed conflicts
d. is the genealogy abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: Several English monarchs and a nobleman perished in battles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts D inside WARS to give WARDS after E and D.
explanation.definitionFit: England has had eight kings named Edward, so several of its kings, as a plural name.

clue.text: Awful deeds and situations offering no way out

indicators.note: awful says the letters of the words after it are mangled into a new shape

explanation.surface: Terrible acts lead to circumstances with no escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges DEEDS AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead end is a street closed at one end, and figuratively a situation with no prospect of progress.

clue.text: Court champion dined with king repeatedly

parts.note: fed is the past tense of feed, to dine

indicators.note: repeatedly says the royal abbreviation appears twice over

parts.note: ER is Edward Rex, the Latin for King Edward

explanation.surface: A winner at court had dinner with the monarch time after time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests royalty, but it is a tennis court. ER usually means the Queen, but R is rex, so it serves for king too.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger Federer won twenty Grand Slam singles titles on the tennis court.

clue.text: Sport needing extra time in later part of day

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for time inside the word for later part of day

parts.note: evening is the later part of the day

explanation.surface: A game going into extra time late in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing extra ... in' adds T inside EVENING; extra time sounds like football but is just the letter T. Eventing is the equestrian triathlon of dressage, cross-country and showjumping.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventing is an equestrian sport combining dressage, cross-country and showjumping.

clue.text: Inauspicious jingle?

definitions.meaning: an advertising jingle is a verse for an ad

explanation.surface: An ill-omened bit of rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whimsical second sense: split as AD VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse conditions are unfavourable or harmful, which is what inauspicious means.

clue.text: King, for example, and brave jester

parts.note: to brave a danger is to face it
a card is a joker or comic person

explanation.surface: A monarch, say, and a bold court fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King, for example' is the playing card, not a ruler; 'brave' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Court cards with faces, namely king, queen and jack, are called face cards.

clue.text: Land being consumed by fire

definitions.meaning: to come down and settle, as a bird does

explanation.surface: Ground that is burning.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to land after flight, and something alight is burning.

clue.text: See 12
Pulse is fast — over one-fifty

indicators.note: over places the fasting season above the numerals in this down answer

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
I is one and L is fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A heartbeat is rapid, beyond one hundred and fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' and 'fast' suggest a racing heartbeat; pulse is the edible seed and fast is the Lenten one.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are the edible seeds of legumes, and the lentil is one of them.

clue.text: King who used rackets to secure a score of titles

definitions.text: King who used rackets to secure a score of titles

parts.words: King who used rackets to secure a score of titles
parts.note: not a crooked monarch running rackets, but a tennis player surnamed King who won twenty Wimbledon titles

explanation.surface: A ruler who ran criminal rackets to grab twenty honours.
explanation.walkthrough: Racket means a criminal scheme, but here it is a tennis racket. Billie Jean King won twenty Wimbledon titles in singles, doubles and mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Billie Jean King, the American tennis great, holds a record twenty Wimbledon titles.

clue.text: Friend that puts king in hopeless position

definitions.text: that puts king in hopeless position
definitions.meaning: checkmate leaves the chess king trapped with no escape

explanation.surface: A pal who leaves a monarch with nowhere to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Mate is British slang for a friend, and in chess mate ends the game by trapping the king.

clue.text: Part of Somalia or other country in Africa

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a stretch of letters inside the next word

explanation.surface: A region of one African nation, or a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters lie within so-MALI-a; 'other' because Somalia too is in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked West African nation, distinct from Somalia in the east.

clue.text: Rabble without love for cruel king

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for rabble surrounds the round letter

parts.note: the herd is the common mass of people, the rabble
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A mob lacking affection for a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside: HERD goes around O.
explanation.definitionFit: King Herod ordered the massacre of the innocents in Bethlehem, a byword for cruelty.

clue.text: Celebrate about rise in king's payment to serving man

indicators.note: about says the word for celebrate goes around the word for rise

parts.note: to sing of something is to celebrate it
a hill is a rise in the ground

explanation.surface: Rejoicing over a raise in a royal soldier's wages.
explanation.walkthrough: To take the king's shilling was to enlist: a recruit accepting the coin, an old British unit of twelve pence, was bound to serve.
explanation.definitionFit: The king's shilling was the coin given to a recruit on joining the British army.
